segments.text: Welcome to your daily Robotics News Digest for September 29, 2026.
Today we cover exciting developments from AI safety, major semiconductor deals, and new workhorse robots.
From Humanoids Daily, Figure Joins NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform as Humanoid Deployment Approaches.
This report details Figure's involvement in establishing boundaries for increasingly capable AI agents through a new safety platform.
Figure contributed to combining the OpenShell runtime with Sentry, a monitoring and enforcement layer, within the platform.

The initiative focuses on ensuring the safety and trust of humanoid robots operating in domestic and professional environments by constraining agent actions through runtime controls instead of solely model safeguards.
This collaboration establishes a foundation for trustworthy agent systems where software decisions result in physical actions.
This development indicates a push towards implementing robust safety mechanisms for physical AI systems.
From latent.space, "[AINews] AMD buys World Labs for $8.2B, as Atlas solves sparse reconstruction problem for robotics, design and more".
This report details the acquisition of World Labs by AMD to integrate its spatial AI capabilities.
World Labs developed advanced models for images, video, and spatial reconstruction, culminating in the release of the Atlas model architecture.
Atlas addresses the sparse reconstruction problem through the method of camera view prediction.
This new architecture has demonstrated applications in robotics simulation, design, and real-world reconstruction.
The acquisition significantly expands AMD's standing within the spatial AI sector.
This development signals a major advancement in spatial intelligence for various technological applications moving forward.
From Humanoids Daily, Dyna Robotics teases a new robot built for real work, indicating that a fuller look is forthcoming.

Dyna Robotics has announced the forthcoming unveiling of a new robotic system designed for demanding and detailed tasks, building upon existing commercial deployments and the development of the Dyna-2 model.
This announcement follows Dyna's ongoing work in the field of robotics.
Further details regarding the robot's specific capabilities and intended applications remain undisclosed at this time.
Specifications and launch timelines are yet to be provided by the company.
This development signals further advancements in the application of robotics to complex industrial and detailed work environments.
Industry observers will await further official information regarding the specifications and launch details.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "A Day in the Life of a Roboticist: Charlie Kemp"
details the work of Charlie Kemp, cofounder and CTO of Hello Robot, focusing on the development of mobile manipulators for home and workplace assistance.
The research centers on creating assistive robots designed to facilitate close physical interaction for older adults and individuals with disabilities.

Kemp's work involved developing systems specifically engineered to enable meaningful physical assistance for people experiencing mobility impairments through advanced mobile manipulation capabilities.
This process emphasized the translation of software concepts into tangible physical realities, focusing on the development of systems that provide practical, physical support.
The findings highlight the successful integration of robotics into personal care through direct physical interaction.
The direction points toward further development in human-robot collaboration for assistive technologies.
From MIT News - Robotics, "Powered by muscle cells, a paper-thin robot swims through watery maze".
This report details the development of a soft, muscle-powered swimming robot utilizing a thin film of gel and genetically engineered muscle cells to propel itself through water.
The research involved engineering muscle cells to respond to light stimuli, causing the robot's fins to flap and generate propulsion.
Flashing light directed at the fins allowed the team to control the robot's movement and speed within a watery maze.
The study further explored optimizing the gel's properties and groove shapes to maximize muscle force generation, establishing a foundation for more efficient biohybrid robots.
This work suggests a pathway toward developing highly efficient, biologically inspired robotic systems.
From Humanoids Daily, Delta Intelligence targets energy and infrastructure beyond its household robot demo.
The initial demonstration focused on household tasks, but the company prioritizes energy and infrastructure as near-term deployment targets.

The development involves a head-and-backpack system designed to integrate models onto various humanoid platforms, with the plan to collect whole-body data from the outset to capture coordination beyond simple hand movements.

Future plans include scaling pretraining data, improving reinforcement learning techniques, and conducting outdoor testing in harsh environments to translate demonstrated coordination into reliable work in energy and infrastructure settings.
This work indicates a progression toward applying advanced coordination capabilities to complex physical tasks outside domestic settings.
And that's all the circuits for today's news.
Hope your day runs with smooth, error-free logic.
Until tomorrow, keep building something amazing!
Bye for now.
